Hi Olivia — thanks for the quick turnaround and for sending the questionnaire. Looping in Lauren from Procurement and Ben from Sales so we can get this into the system.

Quick notes after a first pass:
- COI looks current and the limits are within our baseline for standard suppliers. We typically ask for the certificate holder to read exactly: "Redwood Inference, Inc., 1200 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94102" and endorsement for Additional Insured where applicable. Can you confirm the COI lists Redwood Inference as certificate holder?
- For cyber coverage, our security team prefers to see at least $1M limits OR evidence of residual risk controls; if you have a cyber insurance dec page that shows coverage period and insurer, please attach.
- Vendor questionnaire is helpful — procurement will import this into our vendor record.

Lauren — can you confirm what additional clauses we require on the COI for a services supplier? Also advise the fastest route to get a PO issued (we generally use Coupa for new vendors).

Olivia, can you also confirm remit-to details for invoices so AP can set the payment terms?

Thanks for the ping, Jonas. Olivia — welcome. I reviewed the COI and W-9. A few procurement action items and clarifications to avoid back-and-forth: 

1) Certificate holder wording: please update the COI so it lists exactly "Redwood Inference, Inc., 1200 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94102" as the certificate holder. If the insurer can also add "Additional Insured: Redwood Inference, Inc." on the endorsement, that will speed approval for services work.

2) Cyber coverage: the dec page you sent shows $500K. Our baseline for vendors handling telemetry or customer-facing integrations is $1M; if you can't increase limits immediately, please provide supplemental controls documentation (SOC/Security FAQ or a short note on encryption, segmentation, and logging) and we can route to security for a risk exception.

3) Remit/payment details: Olivia, please confirm AP contact and mailing address or ACH details if available. Our standard net-30 applies unless otherwise negotiated by Sales.

4) PO process: Once we have the corrected COI and the W-9, procurement will create a vendor profile in Coupa and issue the PO. Typical timeline is 3 business days after complete docs. If Ben confirms commercial terms (rate card and SOW), we can request expedited PO issuance for an earlier start.

Next steps (proposed):
- Olivia: send updated COI with exact certificate holder wording + remit/ACH details (by EOD Thu 6/11 if possible).
- Ben: confirm SOW/rate card and whether an expedited PO is requested.
- Lauren: will kick off vendor creation in Coupa once updated docs arrive.

If you prefer, I can send a DocuSign PO template and a link to our vendor onboarding intake form.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Sr. Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference
